newsitem.title: UK: Disillusioned platinum sinks to discount to gold.
newsitem.headline: Disillusioned platinum sinks to discount to gold.

text.p: Platinum prices sank below the price of gold for the first time in nearly three years on Friday, indicating a disillusioned market, analysts said.
But it was finding some support at current levels and the discount to gold is unlikely to get much wider, they said.

Platinum closed just $0.50 an ounce firmer than gold at $382.90/$383.90 an ounce after first sinking to recent lows around $380 an ounce. "Classically platinum has gone to a discount to gold only in recessions. But we're not in a recession and it shouldn't be there," said analyst Tony Warwick-Ching of CRU International.
"It's a symptom of a fairly disillusioned platinum market."
Dealers attributed the drop to a sell-off by investment funds after stops were triggered on the Nymex futures market.
"This is a technical move, because there's a dearth of fundamental news," a dealer said.
Platinum prices have been weakening for months in the face of steady supply from major producer Russia and slack supply from key importer Japan.
"It's getting some support technically and because it's flat with gold. It should hold, but if it doesn't then I really don't know where it will head," the dealer added.
Warwick-Ching also noted that the platinum-gold spread was unlikely to widen much more.
"With the dollar strong and the yen weak it means much higher prices in Japan than a year ago. It's a price sensitive market," Warwick-Ching said.
Platinum has been within a $40 premium and $20 discount since January, 1991.
Its biggest premium to gold was $232.55 in August 1986, and since then it was $180 in November, 1988. The biggest discount was $53.70 in June, 1985 and then $20.10 in December 1991.
